preamble: Nasalization of [i] accompanied by lowering to close-mid [ẽ]. In the Swabian dialect of Horb (as described by Kauffmann 1890), every short stressed vowel before a nasal consonant is nasalized, and the height contrast among /i e ɛ/ is neutralized to [ẽ], so historical i in words like springen and bringen surfaces as [ẽ]. Other Swabian descriptions (e.g. Heissel 1935) report the same merger of i-, e- and ę-sounds into ẽ before nasals.

examples.from: /i/ before a nasal, cf. Standard German spring! 'jump!'
examples.note: Regressive nasalization lowers high /i/ to [ẽ]; oral /i/ keeps its quality away from nasal consonants.

examples.from: /i/ before a nasal, cf. Standard German bringt 'brings'
examples.note: Same neutralization of /i e ɛ/ to [ẽ] before a nasal (Kauffmann 1890, as analysed by Kniess 2025).

sources: Kniess, T. B. (2025). Nasalization and Nasal Vowels in the Swabian Dialect of Horb: A Phonological Analysis of Kauffmann 1890. PhD dissertation, Indiana University. https://scholarworks.iu.edu/dspace/items/f9ca887d-4125-46c1-8eb0-933b17f7d00c
context: Short or long stressed /i/ before a nasal consonant (Horb Swabian)
